source: Harland & Wolff Yard Specification No. 401 & Builder Certificate
unresolved_questions: None. Commonly misquoted as 852.5 ft due to confusion with registered length.

92 ft 6 in (28.19 m) extreme breadth over plating; 92 ft 0 in moulded

46,328 Register Tons (4,632,800 cu ft internal enclosed volume)

unresolved_questions: 1,004 GRT larger than Olympic due to enclosed A-deck forward screen and B-deck staterooms.

Bulkhead A to C deck; B to D deck; C through J to E deck; K through P to D deck
unresolved_questions: None. Bulkhead D double protected with bunker passage door.

documented_value: Depth 63 in (5 ft 3 in) amidships, 78 in (6 ft 6 in) under reciprocating engines; 17 transverse divisions; floor on every frame
Length ~300 ft, depth 25 in along the turn of the bilge amidships port and starboard
12 vertical sliding drop doors (cast iron, heavily ribbed) with friction cataracts, magnetic release from bridge, local hand lever, and bilge float release. Drop time 25-30 sec.
unresolved_questions: Warning bell rang prior to and during closure.

documented_value: 29 Scotch marine boilers: 24 double-ended (15ft 9in dia x 20ft long, 6 furnaces each) + 5 single-ended (15ft 9in dia x 11ft 9in long, 3 furnaces each) = 159 furnaces total. Working pressure 215 psi. Natural draught assisted by stokehold forced fans.

Two 4-cylinder, 4-crank triple expansion engines. HP: 54 in, IP: 84 in, two LP: 97 in dia. Stroke 75 in (6 ft 3 in). Stephenson link motion, Brown steam/hydraulic reversing engine. ~15,000 IHP each at 75 RPM.

One Parsons LP reaction turbine driving centre shaft, ~16,000 SHP at 165 RPM. Powered by exhaust steam from reciprocating LP cylinders. Ahead only. Equipped with automatic governor and changeover valves diverting exhaust to condensers when maneuvering/reversing.
Three propellers: Port & starboard wing screws: 3 blades, 23 ft 6 in diameter, cast bronze, outward-turning. Centre screw: 3 blades, 16 ft 6 in diameter, manganese bronze.
source: Harland & Wolff Engineering Order Book 401 & 2022 Magellan Digital Wreck Scan

documented_value: Four funnels, rake 1 in 12 (1 inch per foot aft). Oval section 24 ft 6 in x 19 ft. Height 175 ft above keel. Funnels 1, 2, 3 boiler exhausts (volumetric coal smoke). Funnel 4 dummy casing for turbine room casing exhaust, galley flue, smoking room ventilation (NO coal smoke). Livery: White Star buff with black top (casing ~75% buff, 25% black).
source: H&W Rigging Plan 401 & The Shipbuilder 1911 & Inquiry Report

documented_value: Four 400 kW, 100V DC dynamos driven by vertical 3-crank compound steam engines in separate compartment abaft turbine room. Two 30 kW emergency dynamos on D deck. 10,000 incandescent lamps (tantalum & carbon). 562 electric heaters. 153 motors.

20 boats total: 14 Class A wooden lifeboats (30 ft x 9 ft x 4 ft, 65 persons each); 2 emergency cutters (25 ft x 7 ft 2 in, 40 persons each, swung outboard); 4 Engelhardt collapsible lifeboats (27 ft 5 in x 8 ft, 47 persons each: A & B on officers roof, C & D abreast cutters). 16 sets of Welin double-acting quadrant davits.
192 ft long enclosed steel weather screen on port and starboard forward A deck with 42 large sliding rectangular glazed windows.
source: H&W Drawing Office alterations 1912 & Father Browne photographs

documented_value: 97 First Class staterooms flush to hull, two Parlour Suites (B51/53/55 and B52/54/56) with private 50-ft promenades; Café Parisien on starboard aft; À la Carte Restaurant expanded.
source: RMG First Class Deck Plan (March 1912) & 1912 Inquiry Report

documented_value: Descending Boat Deck to E Deck. English oak boiserie, Louis XIV style, wrought iron balustrades with gilt bronze leaf scroll medallions, Honour & Glory Crowning Time clock carving on A Deck landing, wrought iron and cut glass dome with 50-light crystal chandelier.

documented_value: Located on F Deck starboard side. Moorish / Arabian style cooling room with glazed ceramic arabesque tiles, teak recliners, brass lamps. Heated saltwater swimming bath (30 ft x 14 ft) lined with turquoise tiles.

Located Boat Deck starboard side abaft forward entrance. Fitted with electric horse exerciser, electric camel exerciser, cycling machines with distance dials, rowing machine, punch bag, wall weights. Paneling white painted v-groove wood, parquet floor.
source: Father Browne photographs & Welch photographs & 1912 Inquiry

documented_value: Two steel pole masts with teak poles. Fore mast 208 ft above keel with steel lookout crow's nest at 95 ft above waterline; internal access ladder with openings at C deck and crow's nest. Main mast 202 ft above keel.
5 kW rotary spark gap transmitter and magnetic detector. Silent soundproof room, operator cabin, 4-wire T-aerial suspended between mast spreaders.
First Class French bistro on B Deck starboard aft; fitted with climbing ivy on white wooden trellis, wicker armchairs, round tables, and large rectangular observation windows overlooking the sea.
source: H&W Yard 401 General Arrangement Plan & Father Browne April 1912 photographs
unresolved_questions: Unique to Titanic in April 1912; Olympic received a similar café only in her late 1912/1913 refit.

documented_value: Starboard side Boat Deck abaft second funnel casing; equipped with electric camel, electric horse, two stationary cycling machines with mileage dials, rowing machine, wall bars, and punching bag.
unresolved_questions: None. Photographed by Father Browne on 11 April 1912 showing passengers and physical instructor Thomas McCawley.
